result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers advise keeping conventional status colors and flag the clash between the brand red and the failed state. B goes further: it gives a specific hex value and pill background for all four statuses and sets a clear usage rule (brand red only for actions, failed shown as a pale pill). It also estimates contrast correctly (white on #d93a35 is about 4.6:1) and says plainly that its figures need checking. A names only color families, not exact colors, and stays general on contrast, though it does explain the color-blindness risk well. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers advise against brand-derived status colors and flag the clash between the red button and the failure red. Answer A goes further: it gives exact hex values for text and pill backgrounds, assigns an icon to each status, and gives a usage rule. It also estimates contrast and says it could not run a checker; its 4.6:1 figure for white on the brand red is correct. Answer B stops at color families and only offers to supply hex values and contrast checks later, so it is less useful.
